properties.name: Warkworth Heliport (NZWZ) - Approach/Departure Sector
properties.description:
Please allow two business days for consideration of your flight request.


This zone is generally restricted to Part 102 operations only.


For approval, all Part 101 flight requests must include:

  • An additional observer’s name and contact details.
  • An attached copy of your CAA Part 101 acceptable pilots certificate.


All Part 102 flights must follow your CAA certificated Operations Specifications.


Operators must maintain a continuous listening watch on the VHF aerodrome traffic frequency (Warkworth Traffic 119.1) and cease operations if a helicopter is approaching or departing from the aerodrome.


Northern Rescue Helicopter Ltd whitelists operators for automatic approval of flights within this zone. For consideration, please supply a copy of your pilots certificate and supporting documents to rpas@northernrescue.org.nz along with the zones you wish to operate within.

properties.name: Take-off and Landing Zone
properties.description:
This zone is established to protect the safe operation of crewed aircraft and to ensure the safety of all airspace users.


Drone operations within this area can be accommodated with the prior approval of NZMB. To request access, please log your flight with at least 48 hours' notice. This advance notice is appreciated, as our team members are frequently engaged in flight operations and may not always be immediately available to respond.


To operate within this area under Part 101, you must:

  • Hold a valid unmanned aircraft pilot qualification issued by a NZ CAA-certificated Part 141 organisation. (See list of providers below)
  • Have an observer present throughout the flight.
  • Operate during civil twilight hours (daytime), unless you hold a valid night rating.
  • Remain below 400 feet above ground level.
  • Obtain approval from NZMB before commencing operations.


If you hold a valid Part 102 certificate that specifically authorises operations within 4 km of an aerodrome, we encourage you to contact us. We are committed to working collaboratively with operators to facilitate safe and efficient operations for everyone using the airspace.


For urgent operational matters, please contact Richard Milner on +64 21 725 104. If he is unable to answer, he may be in flight, so please send an SMS and he will respond as soon as practicable.


Approved Pilot Qualification providers:

  • Fenix UAS
  • RPA Skills
  • FlyUAV
  • Drone Trust / FTNZ
  • Massey University
  • Dronezup
  • Aviation Training NZ

properties.name: Southern Automatic Authorisation Zone
properties.description:
Unmanned aircraft operations in this area are approved, provided the following conditions are met:


Part 101 Operators

Operations must comply with NZ CAA CAR 101.205 and NZ CAA CATI-101.205.

In particular:

  • The pilot must hold an unmanned aircraft pilot qualification issued by a NZ CAA-certificated Part 141 organisation. (If you are unsure what this qualification is, it is unlikely that you hold it.) (See a list of those providers below)
  • An observer must be present at all times while the drone is in flight. The observer must be a person other than the pilot.
  • Operations must be conducted during daylight hours and at an altitude of no more than 400 feet above ground level.

This approval is granted on the basis that all of the above requirements are met.


Part 102 Operators

Operations must be conducted in accordance with the operator’s NZ CAA Operations Specifications and associated Exposition.


Approved Pilot Qualification providers:

  • Fenix UAS
  • RPA Skills
  • FlyUAV
  • Drone Trust / FTNZ

properties.name: Northern Automatic Authorisation Area
properties.description:
Unmanned aircraft operations in this area are approved, provided the following conditions are met:


Part 101 Operators

Operations must comply with NZ CAA CAR 101.205 and NZ CAA CATI-101.205.

In particular:

  • The pilot must hold an unmanned aircraft pilot qualification issued by a NZ CAA-certificated Part 141 organisation. (If you are unsure what this qualification is, it is unlikely that you hold it.) (See a list of providers below)
  • An observer must be present at all times while the drone is in flight. The observer must be a person other than the pilot.
  • Operations must be conducted during daylight hours and at an altitude of no more than 400 feet above ground level.

This approval is granted on the basis that all of the above requirements are met.


Part 102 Operators

Operations must be conducted in accordance with the operator’s NZ CAA Operations Specifications and associated Exposition.


Approved Pilot Qualification providers:

  • Fenix UAS
  • RPA Skills
  • FlyUAV
  • Drone Trust / FTNZ
  • Massey University
  • Dronezup
  • Aviation Training NZ

properties.name: Take off and Landing Protected Zone
properties.description:
This area is protected to ensure the safe take-off and landing of aircraft.


You will be unable to log your flight if it is in this area. Please contact us on requests@eagleflight.co.nz


Flights within this area may be approved for both Part 101 and Part 102 UAS operators with the prior approval of the heliport operator.


Operators will be whitelisted on a case-by-case basis for the period required, provided no aircraft operations are planned at the time of the proposed UAS flight. Please note that approvals may be withdrawn if operational requirements change.


Please provide at least 48 hours' notice for all requests. Our staff are frequently involved in flight operations and may not be at their computers to process requests at short notice.


Ongoing or permanent whitelisting is not available, so please do not request it or be offended if we decline.


Part 102 operators must operate in accordance with their CAA issued Operations Specifications and their Exposition, and obligations under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (HSWA). Approval to fly in this area does not remove the requirement to engage with us to discuss any operational or safety concerns.


All UAS operators must also hold a New Zealand-issued pilot qualification from one of the following organisations:

  • Fenix UAS
  • RPA Skills
  • FlyUAV
  • Drone Trust / FTNZ
  • Massey University
  • Dronezup
  • Aviation Training NZ


Part 61 pilot licences and Wings badges are not accepted as evidence of UAS pilot competency for operations in this area.


For urgent operational matters, please contact Richard Milner on 021 725 104.


Thank you.
